title: Köszönés: tegezés és önözés
summary: Hungarian greetings change with the time of day and with how formal you are. Pick the wrong one and you sound either rude or stiff.

sections.text: Hungarian has two ways of addressing someone. **Tegezés** uses *te* (informal: friends, family, children, often colleagues and young people). **Önözés** uses *Ön* (formal: strangers, older people, shops, offices). The textbook marks them **I** and **F**.
**Szia** means both hello and goodbye. Use **Sziasztok** when speaking to more than one person.

**Csókolom** (“I kiss it”) is what children say to adults, and what some people say to older women. **Kezét csókolom** (“I kiss your hand”) is an old-fashioned polite greeting to a woman. You will hear both, but you don't need to use them.

The full greeting is “Good morning **I wish**” (*Jó reggelt kívánok*). The greeting is the **object** of *kívánok*, so it gets the object ending **-t**: reggel → reggel**t**, nap → nap**ot**, este → est**ét**. The short forms keep the -t.

items.hu: Jó napot kívánok! Kovács Péter vagyok.
